Now the company is tapping Oracle's cloud as another avenue for selling TPUs as it tries to bolster competition with Nvidia in the AI chip market. Thomas Kurian, Google's cloud boss, spent over 20 years at Oracle before joining Google in 2018. In this article GOOGL ORCL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Thomas Kurian, chief executive officer of cloud services at Google LLC, speaks during the Google Cloud Next event in San Francisco on April 9, 2019. Michael Short | Bloomberg | Getty Images Google has spent years pitching customers on the advantage of buying its chips, models and cloud services in one place, offering a full stack that rivals Amazon and Microsoft have tried to replicate. Now, the company is pushing its equipment outside of its own walls to reach more customers and build a bigger business around artificial intelligence chips, a market that Nvidia has dominated. A day ahead of its third-quarter earnings report, Alphabet said on Tuesday that Oracle will offer Google's tensor processing units, or TPUs, the custom chips the internet giant has been developing since 2013 . It's the first time customers will be able to access TPUs outside of Google's infrastructure, and shows that cloud boss Thomas Kurian, who previously spent more than 20 years at Oracle, is looking elsewhere for growth. "They're a very strong competitor, and it's very possible that they could eventually take market share from Nvidia," said Chris Ballard, managing director of Check Capital Management, referring to Google's position in chips. Kurian, who joined Google in late 2018, is operating from a position of strength. Analysts expect Google Cloud revenue to jump about 90% from a year earlier, after growing 82% in the second quarter , with TPUs contributing to its momentum. "Google was great at doing its own thing, but it was never able to serve customers," said Uday Cheruvu, a portfolio manager at Harding Loevner, which owns Alphabet shares. "That mindset has changed." watch now VIDEO 1:14 01:14 Wall Street expects Google Cloud growth to top 90% as Search slows Closing Bell Google opened up TPUs to outside data centers in the second quarter, before this week's announcement with Oracle. Estimates for the TPU business vary widely, but they all point to significant growth. TD Cowen models $9.4 billion in TPU sales for the second half of this year and $62.5 billion for 2027. Wells Fargo expects about $9 billion in third-quarter sales and $99 billion next year. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said on the last earnings call in July that only a small portion of TPU revenue from existing agreements will be recognized this year, with the "vast majority" coming in 2027. She also said Google planned to use more outside capacity in the third quarter while the company builds out its own infrastructure. With $25 billion in second-quarter cloud revenue, Google trailed Amazon Web Services at $42 billion and Microsoft Azure at $29 billion. But Google is growing the fastest. "It's almost like the bigger the pie is getting, the faster they're accelerating into it," said Ballard, whose firm owned about $236 million in Alphabet stock as of June 30. 'Optimize the whole stack' While Kurian aims to get more TPUs into the market by turning to outside partners, he has to balance the benefits of building the customer base with his company's own technology needs. At a Goldman Sachs conference in September, Kurian said Google's AI servers pay for themselves in under two years, and servers running its own silicon reach payback in roughly half that time. "It's because we can optimize that whole stack," Kurian said. Industry research SemiAnalysis estimates that Google's latest Ironwood TPU costs about 44% less to own and operate than an Nvidia GB200 server. There's also the margin hit that comes with external TPU sales. TD Cowen estimates a 20% operating margin on TPU sales, compared with an overall cloud margin of about 35% last quarter. Cheruvu said he doesn't think Google's cloud operating margin could widen much beyond the mid-30s. Google declined comment. watch now VIDEO 1:36 01:36 Why Anthropic’s IPO is risky business Tech Google's biggest TPU customer is one of its top AI competitors. Anthropic, whose Claude models compete with Gemini, agreed last October to use up to 1 million TPUs in a deal worth tens of billions of dollars. Mizuho says that agreement brings nearly a gigawatt of capacity online this year and describes the relationship as Google "arming its closest model competitor." OpenAI is also planning to buy TPUs from Google, CNBC confirmed after The Information first reported on the ChatGPT maker's intentions on Tuesday. Anthropic is getting outside help to finance its Google silicon. This week, Broadcom , which works with Google on TPUs, detailed a $63 billion vehicle backed by Blackstone and three big banks that will buy TPUs and networking gear from Broadcom and lease them to Anthropic for five years. According to analysts from William Blair, the financing plan covers about half of Anthropic's 2027 needs, which suggests more financing is coming. In its IPO filing on Monday, Anthropic said it uses silicon from Google, Amazon, Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices , allowing the company to "select chips based on the best price-performance and efficiency characteristics for each workload." Regarding Google and Broadcom, Anthropic said the partnerships "provide us with access to compute capacity powered by Google TPUs across multiple generations of the TPU platform." Michael Wayland / CNBC European car giant Stellantis reported a 4 billion euro ($4.5 billion) cash shortfall in the third quarter as it ploughed ahead with its $70 billion turnaround strategy to restore profitability. Third-quarter revenues rose 1% to 37.6 billion euros from a year ago, the Chrysler and Jeep owner said on Wednesday, while adjusted operating income rose 184% to 256 million euros from 90 million euros a year earlier. The company also reported that negative industrial free cash flow improved to 4 billion euros, up from 4.3 billion the year prior. Stellantis shares were up 3.6% shortly after the European market opened, but have declined 62% since the beginning of the year. Stellantis stock since the beginning of the year. The announcement came as the transatlantic company continues to implement a 60 billion euro ($66.7 billion) turnaround strategy after years of sales declines, especially in North America. Stellantis reaffirmed that it expects positive industrial free cash flow in 2027 "During the quarter, we continued to make progress in the early execution of our FaSTLAne 2030 plan, launching new products, accelerating partnerships as planned, and delivering meaningful improvements in manufacturing and quality," Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa said in the report. In May, Filosa laid out a five-year plan to achieve positive free cash flow by 2027. This includes investing 36 billion euros in its portfolio of automotive brands, with 60% of the cash to go towards its struggling North America sector. It also plans to introduce new vehicles, refresh models, and incorporate new technologies in its products. China competition European carmakers, including Stellantis, have been struggling in China as domestic brands like Xiaomi, BYD and Geely gain ground and intensify competition. Just this week, German luxury carmaker Porsche said it would reduce its exposure to China as car sales decline in the region. Meanwhile, Mercedes-Benz said its third-quarter car sales slumped due to a "challenging market environment," in the country. Performance was also boosted by strong inflows into its global wealth management business. With the integration of former rival Credit Suisse “firmly on track” for completion by year-end, CEO Sergio Ermotti said the Swiss banking giant remains committed to its global and regional footprint. In this article UBS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT This photograph shows a sign of Swiss giant banking UBS at a branch in Zurich on March 4, 2026. Fabrice Coffrini | AFP | Getty Images UBS reported a pretax profit of almost $3.6 billion in the third quarter, up 27% year over year, largely in line with consensus forecasts. The Swiss banking and asset management giant saw strong net inflows into its global wealth management business. Net profit was $2.7 billion for the third quarter, in line with estimates. UBS shares are up by around a quarter this year The Zurich-headquartered lender's common equity tier (CET) 1 capital ratio — a measure of a bank's solvency — reached 14.7% during the period, up from 14.4% the previous quarter. Strong inflows into its global wealth management business supported performance, with net new assets reaching $55.1 billion by the end of the quarter. UBS recorded $12.5 billion in client commitments across its wealth management and asset management businesses. In its third-quarter earnings statement Wednesday, the bank said the integration of Credit Suisse is "firmly on track" to be completed by year-end, delivering a total of $13.7 billion in cumulative cost savings, above earlier expectations of $13.5 billion. UBS battles with Swiss government over risk tools UBS remains locked in an ongoing wrangle with the Swiss government over proposals for increased capital buffers, aimed at insulating taxpayers from any future banking crisis and contagion from the bank's foreign subsidiaries following the Credit Suisse debacle. The bank is seen as systemically important to the Swiss economy. The country's upper house of parliament voted last month to require UBS to hold 90% of Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital, or about $16 billion in extra shares, as collateral to support its foreign subsidiaries. The level currently stands at around 45%. UBS wants it to be no more than 50%. Speaking with CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" Wednesday, Ermotti said the bank's clients expect it to be competitive. "90% would not, long-term, allow us to be a competitive player," Ermotti told CNBC's Carolin Roth. "I'm very concerned about this development." In an earlier statement, Ermotti said UBS' strong third-quarter performance underlines the benefits of its diversified global business model, adding that the lender remains "strategically committed to its diversified business model and its global and regional footprint." In this article HOOD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Omar Marques | Lightrocket | Getty Images Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets. Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: 51 cents vs. 56 cents expected Revenue: $1.42 billion vs. $1.42 billion expected Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year. Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity. Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings. Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million. Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million. Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading. Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026.
